title: Complex materials engineering via Provenance Action Graphs: potential, structure and demonstration
abstract: arXiv:2610.18314v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This work discusses and tests the potential of reaction graphs for material synthesis, in which events consist of reaction steps (actions) and their outputs (observations). The importance comes from the requirement to synthesize technologically useful materials, especially those that are kinetically stabilized. Often, it is a science that follows years of trial and error, culminating in (published) successful recipes, but is truly driven by far more (unpublished) failures. The entry into the era of AI provides an opportunity to use learning algorithms to encode rules from multi-dimensional synthesis pathways, regardless of their technological usefulness, and to decode both forward prediction and inverse learning modes. The main incentive is to accelerate material discovery by generating a global knowledge base that can be shared among data agents and contributed to by them. translated_title: 基于溯源动作图谱的复杂材料工程：潜力、结构与演示
translated_abstract: 本工作讨论并检验了反应图谱在材料合成中的潜力，其中事件由反应步骤（动作）及其输出（观察结果）构成。其重要性源于合成具有技术用途材料的迫切需求，尤其是那些动力学稳定的材料。这通常是一门需要经历多年试错的科学，最终以（已发表的）成功配方告终，但实际上却是由更多（未发表的）失败所驱动。人工智能时代的到来为利用学习算法从多维合成路径中编码规则提供了机会，无论这些路径在技术上是否实用，并可同时解码正向预测与逆向学习两种模式。主要动机是通过构建一个可在数据智能体之间共享并由其共同贡献的全球知识库来加速材料发现。本文将聚焦于常见合成过程中的几个应用场景。
tldr: 该论文提出用溯源动作图谱表示材料合成过程，通过学习算法从多维合成路径中编码规则并构建可共享的全球知识库，从而加速材料发现。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Provenance Action Graphs to represent material synthesis processes, using learning algorithms to encode rules from multi-dimensional synthesis pathways and build a shareable global knowledge base to accelerate materials discovery.
